papers.title: Investigation of the porosity of parts manufactured by electron beam melting using scanning photothermal radiometry
papers.abstract: In the context of the non-destructive testing of pieces produced through additive manufacturing, this research focuses on investigating porosity using images obtained via scanning photothermal radiometry from Ti-6Al-4V samples. Variations in the material's porosity as a function of the electron beam melting process parameters are revealed through photothermal images. The measured thermal signature is influenced by changes in the material's apparent thermal diffusivity, which is affected by the presence of pores within the bulk material.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究利用扫描光热辐射技术检测电子束熔融Ti-6Al-4V零件孔隙率，但与力学性能及疲劳性能无直接关联。
llm.why_not_core: The paper does not report any mechanical or fatigue data; it only demonstrates a non-destructive porosity detection method without correlating porosity to mechanical properties.

summary_zh.motivation: 针对增材制造零件孔隙率无损检测需求，提出扫描光热辐射成像方法。
summary_zh.method: 利用扫描光热辐射技术获取Ti-6Al-4V样品的热扩散率变化图像，通过热信号差异表征孔隙率。
summary_zh.result: 不同工艺参数下的孔隙率变化可通过热成像反映，热扩散率受孔隙影响。
summary_zh.validation: 通过实验获取光热图像并与工艺参数对比验证方法有效性。

summary_en.motivation: The study aims to develop a non-destructive method for porosity detection in additively manufactured parts using scanning photothermal radiometry.
summary_en.method: Scanning photothermal radiometry was applied to Ti-6Al-4V samples produced by electron beam melting, measuring variations in thermal diffusivity to infer porosity.
summary_en.result: Photothermal images revealed porosity variations correlated with process parameters, as changes in apparent thermal diffusivity.
summary_en.validation: Experimental photothermal imaging demonstrated the method's ability to detect porosity without mechanical testing.

papers.title: Thermal Oxidation Effects on Sub-Surface Microstructure and Mechanical Properties of Cast and Forged α/β Titanium Alloys
papers.abstract: Ti-6Al-7Nb (Ti67) alloy has recently been developed to replace the commercial Ti6Al4V (Ti64) ‎biometallic alloy because of ‎the reported toxicity of the elemental vanadium. Thermal oxidation is an ‎important processing method applied to improve ‎the hardness and wear properties of such titanium ‎alloys. Since the developed alloy, Ti67, contains Nb as beta phase ‎stabilizing element instead of V in ‎case of Ti64, it is expected to behave differently upon processing by thermal oxidation. In ‎addition, this ‎behavior may be influenced by the processing method. Therefore, it is of interest to investigate the ‎influence of ‎thermal oxidation on the surface properties of Ti67 alloy in its forged and cast conditions ‎and compare the results to the ‎commonly used Ti64 alloy. It was observed that the thickness of alpha ‎case formed in Ti64 after oxidation at (1173 K-1373 ‎K) (900-1100 oC) was greater than in Ti67. In ‎addition, the equiaxed microstructure of the forged samples showed a thicker ‎alpha case than the ‎widmanstätten microstructure of the cast samples for the two alloys. Both forged and cast Ti64 showed ‎‎significant improvement in dry sliding wear resistance after thermal oxidation at (1173 K-1373 K) (900 ‎‎°C and 1100 °C), ‎while alloy Ti67 showed less improvement despite the improved surface hardness‎.‎

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文涉及铸造和锻造Ti-6Al-4V的热氧化处理，而非增材制造Ti-6Al-4V的力学或疲劳性能，与用户方向无关。
llm.why_not_core: Does not involve additive manufacturing; studies cast and forged Ti-6Al-4V and Ti-6Al-7Nb with thermal oxidation, not AM mechanical/fatigue performance.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究热氧化对铸造和锻造α/β钛合金表面性能的影响
summary_zh.method: 对铸造和锻造Ti-6Al-4V和Ti-6Al-7Nb进行热氧化处理并测试硬度和耐磨性
summary_zh.result: Ti-6Al-4V的α-case层更厚且耐磨性改善更显著
summary_zh.validation: 通过硬度和干滑动磨损实验验证

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the effect of thermal oxidation on the surface properties of cast and forged α/β titanium alloys.
summary_en.method: Thermally oxidized cast and forged Ti-6Al-4V and Ti-6Al-7Nb and evaluated hardness and wear resistance.
summary_en.result: Ti-6Al-4V exhibited thicker alpha case and greater improvement in wear resistance than Ti-6Al-7Nb.
summary_en.validation: Mechanical testing of hardness and dry sliding wear.

papers.title: Micro-Texture Optimization for Titanium Cutting Tools via Simulation
papers.abstract: This study presents optimization of micro-texture parameters for titanium alloy cutting tools to enhance machining performance.A two-dimensional finite element model was developed in the ABAQUS environment, incorporating the Johnson-Cook constitutive model to simulate the cutting process of Ti6Al4V (TC4) titanium alloy.The effects of micro-texture width, spacing, depth, and distance from the tool edge on cutting force and temperature were systematically investigated using an orthogonal experimental design.Simulation results demonstrated that micro-textured tools significantly reduced cutting forces and temperatures compared to non-textured tools, with optimal parameter combinations achieving reductions of up to 72.6 % in cutting force and 189C in temperature.Range analysis revealed the hierarchical influence of micro-texture parameters: distance from the edge had the greatest impact on cutting force, while texture width most strongly affected temperature.The study reveals critical mechanical-thermal trade-offs in micro-textured tool design, necessitating multi-objective optimization to guide high-performance titanium machining applications.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究的是切削刀具的微织构优化，而非Ti-6Al-4V零件的后处理工艺。
llm.why_not_core: No post-processing treatment of Ti-6Al-4V; focuses on tool design for machining, not on modifying material properties via post-processing.

summary_zh.motivation: 优化钛合金切削刀具的微织构参数以提高加工性能。
summary_zh.method: 使用ABAQUS建立Johnson-Cook本构的二维有限元模型，正交实验设计分析参数影响。
summary_zh.result: 微织构刀具显著降低切削力和温度，最优组合减少切削力72.6%，温度降低189°C。

summary_en.motivation: To optimize micro-texture parameters for titanium cutting tools to enhance machining performance.
summary_en.method: A two-dimensional finite element model using the Johnson-Cook constitutive model was developed in ABAQUS, and orthogonal experimental design was used to study parameter effects.
summary_en.result: Micro-textured tools significantly reduced cutting forces and temperatures, with optimal combinations achieving up to 72.6% reduction in cutting force and 189°C reduction in temperature.
